question.text: A put option exercise allows the AIF to:

answer.text: Put additional money into the investee company
Force the promoter or company to buy back the AIF's stake at predetermined terms
Place the investment in a different fund
Trade options on the stock exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes corporate/promoter buyback as occurring when the AIF exercises a put option on shares held in the investee company. Depending on the put terms, the buyback may be made by the company or by the promoters at a pre-agreed price. The Trap: A put option in this context is an exit mechanism, not an exchange-traded option, an additional capital infusion, or a transfer between funds. Note: Based on workbook page 218 (put option, company/promoter buyback, and put-price terms).
